findings.summary: The code block under "Why is for x in $(cat file) a bug?" is clipped at its right edge, silently truncating both lines.
findings.evidence: Rendered: `for f in $(cat list); do rm "$f"; do` and `# a line 'my notes.txt' deletes two` — source post.json:410-411 reads `for f in $(cat list); do rm "$f"; done` and `# a line 'my notes.txt' deletes two files`; both lines end flush against the dashed block border (~x=1040 of a box ending ~x=1042).
findings.fix: Let this code block wrap or shrink its font so the full 38-char line fits, or re-flow it to the wider left column; the rendered loop currently ends in `do` and is invalid Bash.

findings.summary: Page 1 ends with a `read`/IFS idiom that uses `IFS=` prefixing and `read -r` two pages before either is introduced.
findings.evidence: Final block of page 1: "IFS=: read -r a b c <<< \"$line\"" / "# prefix applies to this read only" — but IFS is first defined on page 3 ("`IFS` = Internal Field Separator.", "Default is space, tab, newline.") and `-r` on page 3 ("`-r` is mandatory: keeps backslashes intact.").
findings.fix: Move this code block onto page 3, directly under the "3. Reading Lines" section, and let page 1 end on the "Memorise One Sentence" takeaway or the single-quote material that page 1 actually defines.

findings.summary: ANSI-C quoting and the single-quote escape-out idiom are demonstrated on page 1 before single quotes, `$'...'`, and adjacent-word concatenation are defined.
findings.evidence: Page 1 shows "echo 'it'\''s'   # -> it's" and "$'\t'                  # a real tab" / "$'\x41' $'\u00e9'" — yet the heading "6. Single Quotes" ("A single quote cannot appear inside, by any means.") comes after them on the same page, "2. Dollar-Quoting" ("`$'...'` is ANSI-C quoting") is on page 2, and "Adjacent pieces join with no separator." is on page 2 under "7. Backslash & Joining".
findings.fix: Reorder page 1 so "6. Single Quotes" precedes the `'it'\''s'` example, and move the `$'\t'` / `$'\x41'` block to page 2 immediately after the "2. Dollar-Quoting" bullets that define the syntax.

findings.summary: The colon-versus-no-colon bullets appear before any default-expansion operator has been shown, so they discuss "the default" with no antecedent.
findings.evidence: Page 5 opens with glob code, then "No colon = only UNSET triggers the default." / "An empty variable stays empty." / "Same switch applies across all these operators." — while "2. Default Operators" (`${v:-d}`, `${v:=d}`, `${v:?msg}`, `${v:+alt}`) and "3. The Colon Switch" table come later on the same page, and the bullets are wedged between two leftover globbing blocks (`find . -name '*.txt'` above, the "Globs Inside Tests" sidebox below).
findings.fix: Delete these three bullets from the top of page 5 and attach them to the "3. The Colon Switch" table where `${v:-d}` vs `${v-d}` is actually presented; keep the remaining glob blocks contiguous at the top of the page.

findings.summary: An indirect-expansion example (`${!APP_@}`, `${!n}`) is given on page 5, a page before indirect expansion is defined.
findings.evidence: Page 5 code: "for n in \"${!APP_@}\"; do" / "  printf '%s=%s\\n' \"$n\" \"${!n}\"" / "done          # enumerate config vars" — but "`${!var}` is indirect: var='HOME' yields `$HOME`." and "`${!prefix*}` and `${!prefix@}` list names by prefix." appear on page 6 under "4. Length & Indirection".
findings.fix: Move the enumeration code block to page 6 so it sits immediately after the "4. Length & Indirection" bullets that introduce `${!var}` and `${!prefix@}`.

findings.summary: Three bullets about newline safety and fork cost sit on page 5 with nothing on the page for them to refer to.
findings.evidence: Page 5 bullets: "Safe with newlines in filenames." / "No fork means no process-creation cost." / "A loop of `basename` pays milliseconds per iteration." — neither `basename` nor any `${path##*/}`-style operator appears until page 6 ("${path##*/}    # basename, no fork"), and the "Zero Forks" callout that states the same claim is on page 7.
findings.fix: Move these bullets to page 6 directly beneath the "2. Path Surgery" code block, where `${path##*/}` / `${path%/*}` give them a referent.

findings.summary: Page 6 makes claims about `${v@Q}`, `${v@A}`, and case modification before page 7 shows what those forms are.
findings.evidence: Page 6 bullets: "Case modification needs Bash 4+." / "`${v@Q}` is the correct way to build a string for `eval` or `ssh`." / "`${v@A}` emits a reusable declaration." — the forms themselves (`${v^}` `${v^^}` `${v,}` `${v,,}`, `${v@Q}`, `${v@U}` `${v@E}`, `${v@A}`) are only tabulated on page 7 under "4. Case And @ Transforms".
findings.fix: Move the "4. Case And @ Transforms" heading and table from page 7 to page 6 ahead of these bullets, so the syntax table and the commentary on it stay together.

findings.summary: The annotation claims an unquoted variable in a redirection is inherently an "ambiguous redirect", but Bash only errors when the word expands to zero or more than one word.
findings.evidence: Code: "> $file    # unquoted: ambiguous redirect"; repeated on the Gotchas page as "Unquoted redirection: 'ambiguous redirect' error." With `file=out.txt`, `> $file` works normally.
findings.fix: Reword to "# ambiguous redirect if $file is empty or splits into multiple words — write `> "$file"`", and fix the matching bullet on the Gotchas page the same way.

findings.summary: The read loop is labelled "the only correct loop" but silently drops a final line that has no trailing newline.
findings.evidence: Code: "while IFS= read -r line; do / printf '%s\n' \"$line\" / done < file        # the only correct loop" — `read` returns non-zero at EOF on an unterminated last line, so the body never runs for it.
findings.fix: Use `while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]; do ... done < file`, or drop the "only correct" claim and add a bullet about the unterminated-final-line case.

findings.summary: The matrix caption renders outside the table frame, appearing as a borderless third cell hanging off the right edge of the box.
findings.evidence: post.json:438 caption `x='' then f $x vs f "$x"` is drawn at x≈872-1040, to the right of the bordered 2-cell matrix (`$x: zero args` | `"$x": one empty arg`) whose frame ends at x≈866.

findings.summary: In the "The Shell Expands, Not ls" flow diagram, a connector edge is drawn straight through two node labels, striking the text through.
findings.evidence: A horizontal line at y≈1211 runs across the interiors of the `matches names` and `builds argv` boxes, crossing both labels mid-glyph so they read as struck-through.

findings.summary: The `${v:+alt}` table row says the alternate appears "only if set", but the colon form requires the variable to be set AND non-empty, contradicting the colon-switch section on the same page.
findings.evidence: Table row: ["`${v:+alt}`","alt only if set"] — while the adjacent rows are precise ("`${v:-d}`","d if unset or empty") and the next section states "No colon = only UNSET triggers the default."
findings.fix: Change the row to "alt only if set and non-empty" (and note that `${v+alt}` is the form that fires on any set variable, including an empty one).

findings.summary: `[[ ... ]]` is used as a test construct on pages 5 and 7 but is not characterized until page 8.
findings.evidence: Page 5 sidebox: "`[[ $f == *.txt ]]` glob-matches."; page 7 callout: "`cmd=(rsync -a); [[ $dry ]] && cmd+=(--dry-run)`" — the first explanation, "Prefer `[[ ... ]]` in Bash." / "No word splitting or globbing on operands.", appears at the bottom of page 8.
findings.fix: Add a one-line gloss to the page 5 sidebox (e.g. "`[[ ]]` is Bash's test keyword — shell syntax, so no splitting on its operands; full treatment in the gotchas chapter") so the construct is explained at first use.

findings.summary: The only Bash-version caveat given is "Bash 4+", which understates the floors for the `@`-transformations and `mapfile -d` presented alongside it.
findings.evidence: Bullets: "Case modification needs Bash 4+." / "`${v@Q}` is the correct way to build a string for `eval` or `ssh`." / "`${v@A}` emits a reusable declaration.", plus the next page's table row "`${v@U}` `${v@E}`" and code "mapfile -d '' files < <(find . -print0)". Per the Bash NEWS file, the `${parameter@spec}` family (Q, E, A) arrived in Bash 4.4 and `U`/`u`/`L` only in Bash 5.1; `mapfile -d` is also 4.4+.
findings.fix: Split the caveat: "`${v^^}`/`${v,,}` need Bash 4.0; `@Q`/`@E`/`@A` and `mapfile -d` need 4.4; `@U`/`@u`/`@L` need 5.1."

findings.summary: Section numbering runs backwards across the page break: "5. Element-Wise On Arrays" on page 6 precedes "4. Case And @ Transforms" on page 7 within the same chapter.
findings.evidence: Page 6 headings run "1. Trim From The Ends", "2. Path Surgery", "3. Search & Replace", "5. Element-Wise On Arrays"; page 7 then opens with "4. Case And @ Transforms".
findings.fix: Renumber so the chapter reads 1 Trim, 2 Path Surgery, 3 Search & Replace, 4 Case And @ Transforms, 5 Element-Wise On Arrays, with the sections placed in that order.

findings.summary: The arrays chapter restarts its section numbering mid-chapter, giving page 7 two sections numbered 1.
findings.evidence: Page 7 headings run "1. Declare And Index", "2. [@] Versus [*]", "3. Count, Indices, Append", then "1. Loading From Files"; page 8 continues the same chapter with "4. Associative Arrays".
findings.fix: Renumber "1. Loading From Files" to "4. Loading From Files" and "4. Associative Arrays" on page 8 to "5. Associative Arrays".

findings.summary: The callout says quotes are optional in array subscripts, but a subscript in an `unset` argument is a normal word that still undergoes pathname expansion.
findings.evidence: Callout "Numeric Contexts": "Inside `$(( ))` and array subscripts, splitting does not happen. Quotes are optional there." — yet `unset arr[1]` (used verbatim on the Arrays page: "Indexed arrays go sparse after `unset arr[1]`") glob-expands `arr[1]` to a file named `arr1` if one exists in the cwd; this is ShellCheck SC2184.
findings.fix: Restrict the claim to subscripts inside `${...}` / `$(( ))`, and add "quote subscripts passed as command words: `unset 'arr[1]'`"; update the Arrays page bullet to the quoted form.
